Apply the existing nearest-neighbor thumbnail reduction first, then convert and copy only the thumbnail. Explicitly close owned intermediate images and retain the caller's image.

Deadline interpretation recognized only some unlimited aliases. `Unlimited / Accuracy` could fall through to a finite deadline, and nonfinite numeric fields could interfere with the fallback. Auto Sketch could trim an explicitly unlimited mode when the separate Boolean flag was absent. Interpret the supported unlimited/off aliases consistently, reject nonfinite/overflowed deadline evidence before trying fallback fields, and preserve unlimited Auto Sketch behavior.

Selecting explicit Pixel Art could retain a stale outline flag and a low resolved stroke cap from a previous mode, changing the requested rendering behavior. Clear the incompatible outline and resolved-cap values in the derived Pixel Art policy while retaining independent safety settings and leaving the caller's options unchanged.

Auto Sketch retained image buffers from rejected planner/finisher trials and could publish a trial after late cancellation. Closing every object recursively would be unsafe because plans can borrow the caller's source or share a preview with the next trial. Release only explicitly owned plan-image fields, preserve caller/input-option images and assets retained by the next or returned plan, and release discarded/aborted trials on every exit path. Check cancellation after planners/finishers and during reduction.

Auto Sketch accepted negative estimates as fitting and could let NaN/Infinity/coercible estimates corrupt its trial selection and trimming arithmetic. Require finite nonnegative real estimates from both planner and finisher, including unlimited mode. Invalid estimates fail while the discarded owned image buffers are released.

`AdaptiveDeadlineRenderer` initially charged each used palette color once. Progressive phases can revisit a color several times, and ordered cursor travel was not fully reflected in the accepted final budget. Custom-color dialogs and verification associated with those revisits were also undercounted. After phase and local ordering, price every actual color transition, its applicable custom-color and verification costs, and screen-coordinate travel. If the ordered plan does not fit, remove complete low-value paths with neighboring transition/travel deltas, preserving the retained geometry and order. Report the actual transition counts and ordered-delivery costs.

Each candidate path separately resolved delivery policy, delays, speed and precision in the adaptive deadline cost loop. This repeated the same configuration work thousands of times for one plan. Resolve one timing context per planning operation and pass it to individual path-cost calculations. The standalone helper still resolves its own context when no context is supplied.

Cancellation after the initial deadline geometry scan could be ignored during importance analysis, selection, local batching and final budget fitting. An interrupted fill estimate could also be swallowed by a general fallback. Check cancellation between and within these late stages, propagate interrupted fill estimates, and check before publishing the final plan.

Region fill safety arithmetic accepted NaN evidence. A fixture with NaN safety/density was assigned risk 0.035, confidence 0.965 and a safe verdict. Coercible or invalid area/perimeter evidence could enter the same calculations. Validate finite safety/density values in [0,1] and positive integral area/perimeter evidence before computing risk or pricing a candidate. Invalid evidence keeps the region on the stroke fallback and cannot approve fill.

Invalid cached fill execution costs, including NaN, could be treated as a zero-cost fill or otherwise corrupt estimates. Accept only finite valid stored core/total/batchable costs; recompute an invalid cache entry from geometry and the execution model.

Region fill evaluation repeatedly constructed calibration/cost models per region and seal, sometimes computing the same seal cost twice. One operation could therefore also mix calibration snapshots. Lazily acquire one execution-cost model per candidate/estimate operation and reuse it throughout region, seal and batchable calculations. Use that model's metadata and retain the existing conservative fallback if construction fails; propagate cancellation.

Gartic canvas detection selected the highest-scoring candidate before checking whether it met the applicable evidence thresholds. A high-scoring unqualified frame candidate could hide a lower-scoring eligible white canvas and return no detection. Rank eligible candidates separately from the best overall diagnostic candidate. Keep all existing confidence/frame/white evidence thresholds.

`min_canvas_area_ratio` affected one candidate search floor but was absent from the final acceptance gate, which always used 0.055. Asking for a minimum ratio of 0.5 could still return a smaller canvas. Validate a finite requested ratio in [0,1] and apply the stronger of it and the existing minimum to final acceptance.

Every Gartic frame and white-evidence sample converted the whole screenshot to RGB, even when it already was RGB. Candidate scoring multiplied those full-screen copies. Borrow an existing RGB screenshot for sampling and the detector; convert non-RGB input once with explicit ownership.

Canvas analysis could not be stopped while constructing masks, flood-filling a large connected region or scoring candidates. Add cancellation before analysis and at bounded row/flood/scoring intervals. Root's browser calibration and detection worker forward their existing callbacks and preserve `InterruptedError`.

Hybrid/sketch previews used drawing endpoints that made a one-pixel dot cover 2×2 pixels and gave fill spans an extra row/column. Preview scaling did not consistently match nearest-neighbor scaling of source pixels, and sketch preview ignored an entry's brush override. Share exact source brush rectangles with simulation and project each inclusive pixel interval to its nearest-neighbor destination interval. Honor each entry's brush and phase filter. Draw directly into the bounded preview rather than allocating a source-sized raster. Forward cancellation through phase previews and root finalization; close already generated owned layers when a later layer fails or Stop arrives.

Optional GPU setup could upgrade pip/remove an existing CuPy distribution before discovering that its shipped requirements were missing or empty. `GpuSetupRuntime.checked_requirements` validates a bounded, nonempty UTF-8 requirements document before any package mutation. `AutoGpuSetup` also requires the supported CuPy distribution to be present before conflict removal; both installers use the preflight.

CUDA setup accepted one correct value from a 32-element test, and runtime status downloaded a sample without verifying the arithmetic. `GpuHardware.cupy_smoke_test` verifies the complete expected output; `GpuBackendStatus._cuda_probe` checks all 256 finite arithmetic results before reporting a working backend. A partially working or wrong kernel does not establish readiness.

An explicit CUDA status could reuse indefinitely cached free-memory, availability and driver-health information. `GpuBackendStatus` refreshes the current CUDA context/metadata on every explicit-CUDA status call, reusing only a successful arithmetic probe for 30 seconds and the same actual runtime ordinal. An unreadable identity disables probe reuse. The cache is locked, bounded to 32 records and returns independent data.

Runtime budget floors could increase a small or zero free-memory allowance, pool limits ignored live allocations and simulation batches assumed at least 128 MiB. `GpuAcceleration.available_vram_mb` accounts for pool-live and reusable bytes once. Runtime pool/tile/score planning and `PixelAccuracyGpu._plan` respect the remaining capacity without artificial minimum budgets. A zero pool limit is rejected because CuPy interprets zero as unlimited; work unable to fit one row plus its halo takes the controlled memory-failure path.

One temporary allocation failure permanently disabled the legacy CUDA backend for later, smaller work. `GpuAcceleration._disable_backend` leaves the working backend available after a recognized allocation/OOM failure while still quarantining a genuine driver/runtime failure.

A failed score tile's exception traceback retained device arrays while the retry attempted to trim the pool, so the memory needed for recovery was still live. `PixelAccuracyGpu` isolates score-tile work and clears failed frames, including chained exceptions, before pool trim/retry. Simulation retry uses the same release boundary. The existing completed-tile accounting remains intact.

A failure during the final CUDA score synchronization was ignored and could return an apparently verified score. `PixelAccuracyGpu.score_cuda_host` requires final synchronization to succeed before publishing the score; a late native failure returns the existing CPU-fallback signal.

Private ordinary/pinned host arrays could go out of scope after `cupy.asarray` queued an asynchronous host-to-device copy. `GpuAcceleration._upload_gray` requests a blocking transfer before releasing its private host owner. This is a source-buffer lifetime guarantee; it does not change device selection or hide GPU execution.

Centered-gradient code returned zero at every outer boundary and on an entire two-pixel-wide/high axis, losing real thin-image edges. `ImageGradients.luminance_edges` uses centered interior and one-sided boundary differences, with zero only for singleton axes. `UniversalGpuAcceleration` CPU/CUDA/OpenCL formulas and the coordinated accuracy/planner/shadow/importance fallbacks agree. Nonfinite luminance is rejected before backend dispatch.

RGBA-to-visible-RGB conversion materialized several full float RGB arrays, including unnecessary compositing for opaque input. `UniversalGpuAcceleration._rgba_visible_rgb` uses one owned RGB output, preserves the exact previous arithmetic order for alpha and takes an opaque fast path.

Pairwise OKLab distance allocated an `N×N×3` difference cube and its squared copy in addition to the required result matrix. `UniversalGpuAcceleration._pairwise_lab_distance` computes row chunks with two-dimensional squared-distance scratch storage on CPU/CUDA. The full `N×N` result is still required. Typical chunks use at most 256 rows and 1,048,576 distance cells.

A requested portrait limit below 80 was silently increased; dot mode ignored the caller's stroke cap. `PortraitPlanner` honors strict nonnegative integral limits, including zero, in line and dot paths. Dot generation stops after the requested visible prefix.

CPU portrait contrast performed Python rounding/clamping and list storage for every pixel. `PortraitPlanner._enhance_local_contrast` uses bounded vector chunks with float64 arithmetic and banker rounding, preserving the prior byte result.

Selecting a small portrait stroke budget scored and retained/sorted every candidate, then built a second full remaining-candidate list. `PortraitPlanner._select_tone_candidates` keeps only the best candidates for a small cap and streams evenly spaced coverage. When the requested priority set is large, it uses a full sort to avoid the heap's measured near-full-selection penalty. Tie order and coverage positions are preserved.

A real `TclError` during root destruction permanently marked the root destroyed, so a later close attempt did nothing while the window could remain alive. `AppBranding._install_destroy_guard` marks successful destruction only after a successful/known-already-destroyed teardown and always releases the reentrancy flag. A real failure remains visible and retryable.

Universal GPU benchmarks omitted source upload, downloaded only a sample and included compilation/startup asymmetrically. The legacy CUDA benchmark also computed huge throughput from a CPU/no-op fallback. `UniversalHardwareBenchmark` warms each workload, times complete input-transfer/kernel/output-transfer work and validates after timing. CPU uses the same workload boundaries. `GpuAcceleration.benchmark` reports zero GPU throughput when the complete GPU pipeline did not run. Profile format 2 invalidates the old incomparable measurements.

Wrong GPU arithmetic could still produce an accepted performance score because only execution/transfer success was checked. `UniversalHardwareBenchmark` validates every warm/timed output against the CPU workload reference: exact categorical palette output, finite shapes and bounded numeric tolerance for float workloads. Bad results remain failed probes.

Direct benchmark calls could report the requested size even though stimulus creation silently used a larger floor, and repeats/size were not consistently bounded. `UniversalHardwareBenchmark._benchmark_parameters` normalizes a strict integral size to 32–1,024 and repeats to 1–5 before stimulus creation and metadata calculation. Top-level small/large benchmark policy remains bounded.

Reading one disconnected OpenCL adapter's metadata before the per-device error boundary aborted discovery of otherwise usable later adapters. `UniversalHardwareBenchmark.benchmark_opencl` reads metadata inside each device's guarded attempt and continues to the next adapter on failure, releasing the completed attempt's resources.

Long hardware/resource benchmark work had no caller Stop callback, and CPU/GPU work could continue through many further phases before the UI regained control. Optional callbacks now reach `UniversalHardwareBenchmark`, `GpuAcceleration` preprocessing/benchmark, `ResourceAllocation.benchmark_allocation`, `ResourceScheduler.benchmark_scheduler` and `PerformanceAutoTuner.run_auto_tune`. They check between workloads/repeats/devices/tiles, within CPU scheduler blocks and before publishing results. Existing `parallel_map` provides queue cancellation. Failed workload frames are released before device cleanup even when the error is retained. Root integrates the UI callbacks.

Tuning saved scheduler/hardware profiles during intermediate phases, so a later failure or cancellation could leave a mixed set of old and new recommendations. `PerformanceAutoTuner.run_auto_tune` computes each phase with `save=False`, validates the final documents and publishes the tuner/scheduler/current hardware profiles through the existing rollback-capable `replace_text_files`. Invalid optional mocked/legacy payloads are not published as auxiliary profiles.

Building the legacy GPU benchmark stimulus allocated a Python integer list for every pixel and spent substantial CPU time outside the measured GPU work. `GpuAcceleration._benchmark_image` generates identical stimulus pixels in 64-row vector chunks, retaining cancellation points and avoiding that Python list.
Enforce background-analysis dimension/pixel caps even for nearly matching sizes, and keep one-pixel axes rather than distorting them to two pixels.
Accumulate minimum background-cluster distances instead of retaining and stacking every full distance plane.
Skip scalar neighbour-distance work for already definite background candidates or rejected edges.
Find connected-component seeds one row at a time instead of materializing two full-image coordinate arrays.
Estimate the removable background from visible pixels composited on white, so invisible RGB values cannot change segmentation.
Count alpha visibility using 256-bin histograms rather than exporting and iterating all alpha bytes in Python.
Bound alpha-combination scratch buffers by rows and use byte-sized feather classification arrays.
Close owned image buffers on success, cancellation and partial failure across image editing, import, exports and subject dialogs, while preserving caller-owned and successfully returned images.
Reject invalid/oversized background-removal sources and nonfinite feather settings before allocating an oriented image.
Reduce the background-analysis proxy before expanding it to RGB, avoiding a full-source RGB intermediate.
Observe Stop between orientation, large upscale/resampling and final conversion rather than continuing expensive work after a request to stop.
Describe premultiplied alpha and palette-embedded alpha correctly, considering only palette entries actually used by the image.
Inspect image transparency without a full-image alpha/RGBA conversion: extrema for alpha, 256 palette entries for indexed images and bounded strips for colour keys.
Classify drawing styles from the visible composited image, ignoring hidden colour under transparent pixels.
Sample drawing-style metrics directly into a bounded image and count colour properties with bounded arrays instead of copying the full source and building Python pixel tuples.
Honor Stop during PNG image/preview encoding, flush and publication-lock waits before replacing the destination; an interrupted export cannot publish a late file or leave an incomplete stage.
Encode preview PNGs in a tracked worker using a snapshot, keeping encoding off the UI thread and preventing later preview changes from altering the exported frame.
Create background-removal Undo state only after successfully adopting a result, rather than when scheduling work that may fail.
A no-op background-removal result retains the current image, valid plan and Undo state instead of invalidating the session.
Reject image edit/Undo/export actions during shutdown before opening dialogs or taking image snapshots.
Validate UI transaction counters and retry limits before mutation or input, so malformed metadata cannot partially change state.
Bound UI transaction history and detail strings while reporting dropped event count and still delivering every observer call.
Record terminal operation/recovery failures as FAILED and preserve the original exception when failure reporting itself fails.
Reject automatic subject detection on fully transparent images rather than interpreting invisible RGB as a real subject.
For partially transparent images without fully empty pixels, estimate the subject from its visible white composite, including indexed-palette transparency.
Sample ordinary opaque subject images before channel expansion and decode alpha in bounded strips, avoiding full-size RGBA/RGB analysis intermediates.
Validate subject-mask dimensions, a 64-megapixel allocation limit and finite normalized rectangles before allocating the mask.
Observe subject-selection Stop during alpha scanning and after explicit ROI allocation or full-size mask expansion.
Show transparent subject-selection and mask previews against their visible white background rather than exposing hidden RGB.
Downsample compatible subject-preview sources before EXIF rotation/conversion, retaining correct rotated bounds and caller EXIF.
Roll back partially built subject dialogs and keep their selection state closed after Apply/Cancel, preventing duplicate callback delivery.
Bind a subject-selection result to its original image and idle operation; late callbacks cannot apply a rectangle to a replacement image or ongoing drawing.
Roll back failed preview-page registration/layout while retaining the previous page, selector state and original error.
Fit initial main/dialog geometry and minimum sizes to the current screen and CustomTkinter window scaling, avoiding oversized mandatory dimensions on smaller/high-DPI displays.

Decode local imports from a private bounded snapshot of the same regular-file handle whose size was checked; actual file growth cannot bypass the byte budget and later path replacement cannot change the decoded snapshot.

Stream encoded image input into a memory-bounded spool and decode base64 in bounded blocks, avoiding full bytearray/BytesIO/encoded-substring duplicates. Reject impossible encoded lengths and invalid budgets before allocation.
Accept the URL-safe base64 alphabet already supported by the drop parser while rejecting invalid padding or hidden trailing encoded content.

Carry cancellation through every import source and after decoding; consume available HTTP body data with read1 so Stop/deadline checks do not wait for a full chunk, and preserve interruption if response cleanup fails.
Validate HTTP Content-Length and verify identity-encoded body length before decoding, while keeping compressed wire length separate from decoded-byte limits.

Run manual/automatic hardware, GPU and resource tests through the shared tracked worker lifecycle; prevent concurrent drawing/tests, snapshot Tk settings before dispatch and reject cancelled late recommendations.

Read the exact deterministic palette-refinement sample through bounded 256 × 256 tiles instead of copying and converting the entire source raster. Sample order, duplicate indices, transparency and original source coordinates are preserved.
Reject invalid palette seeds, wrapped/out-of-range RGB channels, nonintegral or nonpositive palette sizes and oversized seed sequences before refinement allocation.
Weight palette strokes by their covered raster length rather than Manhattan length, which disproportionately favored diagonal strokes when ranking color groups.
Bound reduced-palette merging against every original source color, preventing successive near-color merges from drifting beyond the advertised color-distance limit.
Compute OKLab metrics once per source color and keep one representative accumulator per hue family instead of retaining every family member and calculating the same metrics twice.

Require matching, finite, nonnegative hue weights and valid family limits/chroma thresholds; reject overflowing total mass rather than publishing invalid coverage. Zero mass/capacity avoids color work.
Isolate malformed local settings fields so one corrupt scalar cannot abort unrelated valid preferences; portable imports reject those same invalid domains before publication.
Apply settings as a guarded UI transaction: suppress intermediate profile callbacks and restore prior variables/geometry if a setter fails.
Preserve the selected profile's defaults for absent legacy settings and display extras instead of replacing them with generic fallback values.
Recognize unsupported settings schemas and preserve the existing document through later saves until the user explicitly resets that profile.
Remove consumed legacy setting aliases after migration so portable-profile validation accepts migrated older documents while giving explicit current keys precedence.
Persist and restore the chosen Gartic opacity in the active profile.
Propagate a failed settings save to dependent operations: retain the active profile/selection, and block export or import that would otherwise continue with stale settings.
Reject duplicate canvas fields across portable-profile sections and nonobject canvas sections instead of silently overriding or ignoring ambiguous input.
Prevent profile management while a profile transition is queued/running or the application is closing, keeping the requested identity and stored settings consistent.
Verify/hash/decode a recovery image in a tracked, cancellable worker; apply it only after that worker completes, with a fresh idle/shutdown check after the recovery dialog.
Explicit recovery clearing cancels a queued checkpoint and suppresses re-creation; forget in-memory resume state only after successful deletion.
Disarm native input before recovery profile/settings/image work so an exception during recovery cannot leave the previous armed state alive.
Stream recovery-directory enumeration and filter names before creating Path objects instead of retaining every unrelated directory entry during cleanup.
Respect portrait time semantics: Unlimited does not impose the numeric fallback budget or time-based thinning; short explicit budgets can reduce below the old minimum stroke counts.
Base end-to-end tuner statistics on the visible white-canvas composite, preventing invisible RGB/keyed transparency from being reported as visible chromatic content.
Permit a bounded Pixel Accurate quality rescue for an Unlimited photo plan, rather than treating the absence of a deadline as a one-second budget. The existing target-pixel limit remains enforced.
Quality rescue moves planning resolution upward or preserves Extreme; it no longer downgrades Extreme to Ultra.
Remove a previous Quick Sketch renderer policy when a rescue chooses another renderer, preventing the next planning pass from overwriting the rescue's detail/quality choices.
Planning watchdog Off disables its hidden automatic deadline, while user Stop and the separate bounded dry-run policy remain available. Heartbeat text reports the actual timeout state.
Watchdog fallback preserves explicit Pixel Accurate/Unlimited quality fields, while allowing CPU/GPU execution-route fallback and retaining finite attempt limits when enabled.

Treat a verified, fully completed sequence checkpoint as a completed no-op before target activation, countdown, drawing or post-draw correction; preserve Stop and unconditional input cleanup. An empty remaining sequence no longer falls back to drawing legacy color groups again.

Transfer the filtered visible-color delta back into unassociated source channels while retaining alpha. Unchanged/protected pixels remain byte-exact; invisible source RGB cannot affect visible smoothing.
Assign each ordered-Bayer source pixel to exactly one primary or secondary group. Both palette orders now reproduce the same intended mixture, for serial and worker planners.

Materialize the complete established base colour order, then append the detail pass. Preserve path phase hints, explicit detail brush size and all base geometry. Target and guarded preview must follow this same sequence; existing configured visual verification is retained by the coordinated runtime integration.

Compare the complete candidate route with the supplied route and retain the shorter one. Apply the same nonregression contract to segment and polyline optimizers without changing geometry, structural windows or reversal policy.
Normalize the existing aliases before those planner decisions, so old profiles receive the same planning semantics as their canonical speed.

Keep removal/protected-peak evidence only while the component can still be rejected as small; clear that evidence at the acceptance threshold. The connectivity frontier and seen/output masks remain. Both legacy and Sketch 2.0 implementations share one count.
Compute transitions in blocks of 64 columns, transposed into the same x-major/y-major result order, while keeping the existing area bound.
Stream ranked entries into the bounded heap. Retain protected-prefix priority, stable ties, source order and aligned phase/semantic metadata.
Keep only the best bounded micro-stroke candidates in a heap; prefer two-pixel strokes and then earlier colour/source positions while leaving all longer strokes intact.

The final `ProfilePolish` pass undid `ProfileEngine`'s explicit Pixel Accurate lock and Unlimited time choice in the four core profiles. The engine also failed to preserve the current `Unlimited / Accuracy` spelling. Both automatic passes now share the same protected-setting contract; normal Auto presets and Manual settings retain their behavior.

Region-fill enablement and aggressiveness were absent from the profile-default snapshot. A new target with no settings file could inherit the preceding target's disabled fill engine or Aggressive policy. `ProfileIsolation` now resets these controls and includes the current detail/quick-sketch variables in its shared snapshot. The detail-zoom viewport also resets with the other preview pages.

StudioUI disabled Paint's secondary Prepare Paint & draw button using the obsolete test/lock/preflight sequence even when the controller's primary button and setup wizard allowed preparation. The secondary button now mirrors the controller's actual state. The workspace model has an explicit Paint preparation mode with optional diagnostics; it does not claim `can_test` before calibration exists.
The local F1 help binding conflicted with the global F1 Quick Start binding. Help now uses Shift+F1 and its tooltip identifies both shortcuts.

A single workspace refresh independently checked target locks, preflight and dry-run validity twice for its checklist and wizard. It now reads each once and shares that snapshot, avoiding duplicate calibration-backed validation and disagreement between the two displays during a refresh.

The beginner wizard instructed manual-only targets such as Kleki, Magma and Drawize to use browser Auto setup. It now selects its action and setup label from the actual target capability, and treats optional tool calibration consistently when a palette is already usable.

A successfully unlocked wizard still said that Start was locked and asked for another Unlock. Its status and next action now point to Start while the confirmation is valid, and revert to Unlock when it expires.

Case folding decomposed valid letters such as `ǰ` and `ΐ` after the word guesser's NFC normalization. Its own letter validator then rejected them or miscounted the pattern. A final NFC pass restores canonical letters before validation, indexing and wildcard matching.

CTk sliders/scrollbars wrap Canvas or Frame widgets, so native class-name checks missed their existing wheel handlers and scrolled the surrounding panel as well. The dispatcher now recognizes those actual CTk control classes while walking the event target's ancestors.

On Windows, CTk's one-pixel scroll increment made the coalesced handler move only one pixel per 120-delta notch. The dispatcher preserves CTk's normal 20-pixel distance while retaining fractional accumulation and the bounded 12-notch batch. Generic canvases and macOS/Linux keep their existing units.

Moving the pointer to another panel before the 16 ms wheel flush discarded the first panel's complete queued motion. The dispatcher flushes that motion to its original panel before changing the destination.

A compact sidebar group hid existing controls before packing its new shell. If that pack or a later group's construction failed, the supposed original-layout fallback left controls hidden. Group and whole-install rollback now restore prior packing/options/order and destroy only the newly owned shells. CTk controls retain their logical padding so repacking and profile visibility do not apply DPI scaling twice.

Sidebar discovery repeatedly crossed the Tk boundary for the same text/tree data, and genuine CTk containers without a `text` option raised an uncaught `ValueError`. Installation now indexes the original tree once, treats those containers as non-text widgets, preserves scoped preorder matches, and releases the index after installation.

Preserve the owned press until LEFTUP succeeds. A failed release revokes input authorization, disarm remains unconditional, and a later cleanup or explicit arm retries only the application's pending release.

A per-instance reentrant lock serializes arm, disarm, press, release and move. Disarm waits for an in-flight command, releases an owned button, then revokes authorization before returning. Later ordinary commands see the revoked arm.

`TargetCapture` exposes an optional keyword-only `cancelled` callback. Its cancellable path checks before spawn, polls communication at most every 100 ms, rejects late completed results, and performs bounded terminate/wait/kill/reap cleanup on interruption. Root forwards the callback through four calibration worker call sites; both picture-palette probes before and after RGB calibration also receive it.

Every process failure records its current reason and available output through the existing sanitized, bounded log path. Bytes are decoded before sanitization. Diagnostic-storage failure cannot replace the actual operation exception.

`LocalSanitization` recognizes escaped separators, Unicode escapes and serialized custom home paths. It redacts within quoted-literal boundaries before handling ordinary paths, preserving legitimate apostrophes in names and the surrounding JSON/repr syntax. Escaped quotes cannot start new literals, avoiding repeated rescans of a malformed line.

A manually marked subject rectangle and its mode disappeared on session recovery. Simply saving the rectangle could also bind a new image's selection to an older cached image after a failed image checkpoint. Save validated normalized subject geometry and mode against the cached image's SHA-256. Attach it only to its matching, successfully recovered raster. A weak source reference advances only after successful image publication, while selection-only checkpoints reuse the encoded image. Real application/disk round trips verify exact subject masks, changed-image failure/retry, malformed or mismatched selection rejection and legacy defaults. Recovery remains Manual and disarmed.

Every deadline-sequence path copied the complete remaining suffix and all its dictionaries even when normal, unlimited or throttled policy could not reorder anything. Check the existing eligibility policy before accessing the suffix. Eligible replanning retains its original algorithm and complete metadata. No-tail-access fixtures, 40 seeded active fixtures and an actual unlimited `execute_plan` route verify the adapter. Paired measurements below preserve complete entries and scheduler output.

After a released-mouse pause, the same-color next path trusted cached color/brush state even though the user could change both while paused. Invalidate verification samples on pause, restore the known tool and calibrated brush, reselect the current color and perform the configured ink checks before resumed drawing. Real execution fixtures change color and width during the pause, exercise both legacy and ordered paths, and verify Stop prevents resumed input. Unknown manual tool configuration is not claimed to be detectable.

“Retry correction only” emptied drawing groups but retained executable background/region fill options. It could fill over the existing drawing before scoring a fresh correction. Skip every canvas-clear/fill prelude for the explicit correction-only operation while retaining those descriptions as comparison evidence. An actual retry with both fill types issues only mandatory input cleanup and fresh snapshots when the correction planner declines patch input; ordinary full drawing still fills normally.

The emptied retry retained the original total estimate but set path count to zero. Correction costing consequently used a full drawing's time as the cost of one correction path. Derive a valid per-path reference from the original positive path count before emptying execution. A 60-second/6,000-path drawing supplies 0.01 seconds to the actual correction planner. Fill-only plans provide no fabricated per-path estimate.

Each retry inherited the first drawing's “before correction” metrics, so even a skipped retry could claim the original cumulative improvement again. Shallow-copied mutable runtime counters could also modify the completed plan and carry old results into the retry. Start a new before/after pair and runtime counters for each attempt; preserve the original comparison target and completed plan. Fresh scoring becomes the retry history baseline and is reflected in the current UI result. Actual execution/history tests verify a skipped retry reports zero gain, the original metrics/counters remain unchanged, and stale successful evidence cannot replace a failed fresh capture. The existing failed-evidence trust contract is completed without another ID.

Strict/adaptive ink checks and the retry of a delivery check used the plan's default width, while an ordered entry could have selected a different actual brush. Use the selected execution width for each check. Two-color execution fixtures verify widths 4→1; delivery retry checks use the same current width as the original check. This is the actual mouse verification boundary, distinct from PL31 simulation/cost inheritance and PB03 detail-batch snapshot ordering.

Near-neutral source colors received hue-family penalties in vector/GPU mapping that the canonical scalar matcher explicitly disables below OKLab chroma5. For source `(222,200,194)` and the recorded four-swatch fixture, Faithful scalar matching chose index3 while CPU/vector mapping chose2. Gate the family penalties consistently in universal NumPy/OpenCL, fused CUDA, legacy CUDA array expressions and the Pixel Accurate emergency CPU fallback.

A palette without white used its nearest color as the supposedly untouched white canvas. An empty black-only plan reported100% target/plan accuracy, zero coverage and one missing pixel; black spill also disappeared from the error classification. Use signed `-1` only as internal unpainted-white simulation state when no exact white swatch exists. CPU/CUDA scoring retain missing/spill errors. Corrections repair drawable colors but never emit the sentinel or pretend an unavailable white swatch can erase spill. Preserve explicit valid background indices.

Excluding unpainted white removed isolated colored pixels' boundary evidence. A black dot changed from protected cleanup with micro score.66 to unprotected mid-detail with score.18 solely because Skip white was enabled. Count skipped white/transparent neighbors as boundaries of drawable features, while keeping nondrawable pixels outside contour/protected maps. A singleton target also retains micro-detail evidence.

The picture-palette edge sampler used a clipped Laplacian, which selected only the bright background around a dark accent. Its unchanged filter border also supplied “edge colors” for uniform images. Use symmetric four-neighbor RGB contrast, retaining both sides of real transitions and no artificial outer-border response. Preserve row-major bounded sampling and palette deduplication. Increment the picture-cache schema so previously cached edge choices are rebuilt.

Component extraction issued five NumPy sums plus max/count work separately for every run, including every one-pixel checkerboard component, and kept a second statistics dictionary per component. Reduce busy rows together with bounded start/end reduction arrays. Preserve small slice reductions for rows with fewer than eight runs. Accumulate final component fields directly, retaining exact IDs, runs, order and statistics.

Preview accuracy retained multiple normalized RGB copies and materialized full-frame linear/LMS scratch arrays, alongside already finished metric intermediates. Borrow already valid normalized inputs in read-only numeric consumers, bound CPU OKLab transform scratch to65,536pixels, and release evaluator intermediates when their scalar results are complete. Whole-workload GPU routing and formulas remain unchanged.

HTML drops could select a script URL, a non-image data-src attribute or an image inside a comment/template before the actual dragged image. The parser now reads image elements and visible image links, ignoring inert/comment content and unrelated attributes. Quoted/unquoted attributes are decoded once, and duplicate attributes follow their first value.

A text/uri-list comment containing a short image URL could win instead of the actual dropped URI; multiple file URI lines also required Tcl preprocessing. Standard URI-list lines are now recognized with comments/blank lines excluded, and supported files are found without Tcl splitting.
TIFF, ICO and APNG files already decoded successfully through ImageImport but were rejected by the drop extension filter. File drops and the shared file-picker pattern now admit those same formats.

An inline image was parsed/stat-tested as a filesystem name, creating thousands of Path components from base64 slashes. Repeated case-insensitive matching also processed the case-sensitive base64 body unnecessarily. URI sources now skip filesystem parsing, the body uses its explicit ASCII alphabet, and already matched spans are not rescanned. Ordinary image URLs also skip irrelevant search-query parsing.
An open guide continued showing Paint instructions after a profile change. The current topic now follows the live profile without requiring the user to close the guide or navigate to another page.

Every guide Configure event reconfigured every label and queried the same width per label, including height-only changes. Events now coalesce into one idle callback; an unchanged wrap width produces no label updates.

The guide treated a physical widget width as CTk logical pixels and forced a 240-pixel minimum wrap, allowing text to exceed scaled or compact viewports. Wrapping now divides by the widget scale and fits the available logical width.
Guide navigation required pointer operation of its buttons/menu. Alt+Left/Alt+Right now navigate bounded topics and Escape closes the guide; the shortcuts are visible in the guide.
Reopening an existing iconified guide only raised it and did not request restoration. Reopen now deiconifies and raises the existing window.

Each CTk guide scroll frame installed wheel/Shift callbacks on the root, but destruction left those callbacks and their frame references registered. The scoped frame now removes only its own callback IDs, including partial construction, without unbinding other widgets.

Smart Canvas Drop passed signed desktop positions as Tk geometry offsets; negative offsets actually address the right/bottom screen edges. The overlay is now positioned with typed System32 SetWindowPos calls and checked against GetWindowRect. It stays visually hidden during realization/mapping and is revealed only after verification.

Stop during the screen-area picker's 250ms launch delay did not cancel its independently scheduled overlay; a late selection could still be delivered. The picker now observes the supplied cancellation callback before capture, while open and before delayed delivery, cancels its own jobs, restores prior window states and disposes undelivered crops.

Loading a large custom-profile registry rebuilt the full case-folded name set for each record, producing quadratic startup work. One incrementally maintained set now preserves the same normalized-name and storage-owner rules.

`os.walk` silently ignored an unreadable included resource directory. Source validation could return success and publish a ZIP lacking its theme/assets even though all individually required files existed. `ReleasePackage` propagates included-directory traversal errors in both validation walks and the final inventory. The previous complete archive remains intact and staging is removed. Excluded private trees remain excluded.

`build_exe.py --help`, misspelled flags and unsupported positional arguments fell through to creating a virtual environment and installing/building packages. Parse the supported `--onefile` and `--gpu` options before platform or build side effects. Help succeeds without building; unknown options fail immediately.

The release workflow checked the versioned tag name and draft metadata but not the actual Git ref. GitHub ignores `target_commitish` when a tag already exists, so binaries from the current build could be published under a preexisting tag pointing elsewhere. `ReleaseIdentity` resolves the exact ref, peels bounded nested annotated tags and requires the build SHA. Verification is read-only by default. The workflow may explicitly create only a missing tag at that SHA, re-read creation races, and use `gh release create --verify-tag`. A second read verifies identity immediately before publication. Existing refs are never updated or deleted. The helper is required by source packaging and the source gate.

Main, tag and manual workflow runs used different ref-specific concurrency groups while they could resume the same versioned draft. Their clobbering uploads could interleave, mixing two independent builds' ZIP/installer/checksum/manifest assets. Use one repository release-workflow concurrency group, `cancel-in-progress: false` and `queue: max`. Cooperating publishers run serially without replacing the sole pending request.

The one-shot source hygiene check traversed every private builder/output tree and treated an upstream `check_once.py` inside `.build-venv` or the frozen output as repository source. It also scanned `.git` fully before discarding findings. Prune the same excluded directory names and links as source packaging. Keep genuine source and workflow one-shot detection, reject included-directory traversal errors and avoid per-file metadata queries for irrelevant filenames.

A 120-second manual pause plus the three-second resume countdown made an otherwise completed 0.8-second fake-device run teach both speed and ETA models a 123.8-second duration. The analysis also recommended updating ETA from that idle time. Record each pause explicitly and exclude manually paused runs from throughput, ETA and strategy learning. Keep the honest wall time and canvas-quality analysis, classify pause time separately, and avoid misleading ETA/efficiency recommendations. Actual `execute_plan` and public persistent-model tests prove the exclusion; an uninterrupted run remains eligible and clears old pause metadata.

Strategy feedback counted only the report's `drawn` category as delivered. One hundred clipped or edge-following delivered paths plus one skipped path consequently produced a zero safety-delivery score. Include all three exclusive delivered categories. Tests feed actual `RuntimeSafetySession` output through the public strategy writer and prove equivalent accepted proxy scores for interior, clipped and edge-following geometry. The result remains explicitly labeled a runtime delivery proxy.

Queued worker status/progress could overwrite the explicit Stop status with “Drawing” or “Finished” before the worker exited. Ignore ordinary status/progress after Stop, then confirm the matching worker's exit. Explicit terminal events preserve real failures and the recording tool's intentional Stop-and-save result. Tests cover queued success/progress, unrelated completion, ordinary completion, timeout text and recording success/disk failure.

Export always saved the plan's base preview even when the user was inspecting a different layer, and it could differ from the displayed simulated final. Resolve rendering and export from one shared view map. Export the selected complete original/target/final/heatmap/coverage/safety/detail/stroke/fill/color view with a descriptive PNG name, honor layer toggles, and explain unavailable layers. Actual worker exports are decoded and compared pixel-for-pixel for all 12 views. The modal-time stale image/view checks complete existing lifecycle contracts without extra IDs.

Reset learned draw timing used raw UI options, whereas actual Auto planning records a resolved drawing-style/tool/brush context. Reset could erase a different record and retain both the learned current model and its displayed estimate. Prefer the current plan's effective context only for the same active profile, invalidate its estimate after successful reset, preserve the plan on a failed reset, and prevent reset during an active worker or shutdown. Tests record two real calibration contexts and verify that exactly the effective context is removed.

Image import copied an embedded non-sRGB ICC profile onto unchanged RGB numbers, but planners treated those numbers as sRGB. A generated valid RGB profile with exchanged red/blue primaries imported `(220,40,10)` instead of the independently expected `(10,40,220)`. Convert tagged file and bitmap-clipboard input to sRGB with Pillow's CMS and relative colorimetric intent. Preserve alpha/indexed transparency and the borrowed clipboard image; retag converted output with sRGB so exported/reimported images do not convert twice. Bound profile bytes, explain invalid profiles, retain exact untagged pixels and close cancelled outputs. The source label identifies successful conversion. Tests use a generated ICC fixture and its independent channel mapping; no external binary fixture is downloaded.

Verification flattened clipped paths, copied every adjacent pair and could search the same longest segment three times. When clipping left two isolated dots, its fallback sampled across the undrawn gap. Select the first longest delivered segment once with constant scratch space; fall back to the first delivered dot. Reuse it for delivery, color and exact-color sampling. Preserve path order and native actions, poll cancellation during long paths and many dots, and use pairwise iteration without path slices. A real CanvasGuard/execute_plan regression reproduces two clipped dots and proves that the gap is no longer sampled; an independent brute-force oracle covers ordinary geometry and tie ordering.

Canvas verification accepted RGB band contrast as an edge but located it using luminance only. A real rectangle with outside `(100,100,20)` and inside `(101,69,177)` has equal luminance; all sides were spuriously placed at search offset −24, stopping a correctly selected canvas. Locate adjacent boundaries with weighted RGB contrast, prefer the nearest expected position on exact strength ties and require nonzero local evidence. Existing weak/no-margin fallback and conservative-inset semantics remain.

Custom Auto reserves jumped at policy thresholds. Increasing the timer 30→31,80→81 or150→151 seconds reduced usable drawing time. Interpolate established generic timer anchors continuously, with reserve slope below1 and the existing30-second maximum. Fixed game presets and explicit Off/manual reserves retain their values.

Extra Fast evaluated the same complete final plan twice when every local candidate kept the original paths. The second pass repeated target capping, stroke ordering and stateful costing. Reuse the first complete evaluation only when every source group remains unchanged, including portrait semantics. Changed proposals still receive the complete downstream regression guard; Stop remains observable after the first evaluation.

X11 Gray, Maroon and Purple were displayed using names that parse as different CSS RGB values. Reports could say `Purple → Purple` for a visible color change, and an exact X11 match was labeled CSS. Preserve ordinary CSS input precedence, provide explicit `X11` names for collisions, publish only aliases that parse to the same RGB, and report the vocabulary of exact extended matches. Rendering colors and candidate scoring are unchanged.

Explicit Portrait style injected the full-color `Subject first` policy into Paint's supported current-color shaded renderer. Both Manual and Auto `make_plan` then failed with a subject-focus compatibility error. Do not inject that full-color policy into a compatible single-color portrait. Preserve any explicit user subject selection so the real planner still rejects an invalid combination. Full-color Portrait and Extra Fast's contour policy keep their behavior.

Preview safety treated the fitted image rectangle as the entire canvas. A 1×24 source centered in a 200×48 canvas raised `CanvasSafetyStop` because its fitted width was only 2 pixels, although the actual centered stroke was safe. Ordinary letterboxing also clipped legal image edges and projected saved polygons/anchors against the wrong rectangle. Keep full-canvas guard geometry and centered image placement separate. Project normalized/relative/screen evidence through the complete target canvas; render guarded paths and safety/debug/stroke layers back into the fitted image crop. Root forwards the current planning canvas through ordinary, recursive and test plans.

Both Fill detectors retained every pixel index of a component after it touched the canvas border, although border-connected components are unconditionally ineligible for bucket Fill. A large background therefore retained unusable candidate geometry for its entire flood traversal. Release that list on the first border contact and omit later coordinate retention. Continue the complete traversal, component accounting and bounded cancellation checks. Interior candidate point order and every subsequent safety/contour decision remain unchanged.

A failed palette rescan cleared reviewed colours, and selecting a replacement screenshot bound its new target before detection completed. A replacement now stages detection and the display image, then commits colours, screenshot, preview and anchor together. A failure leaves the old reviewed draft usable. `GetColorPositions.read_snapshot/start_scan`; C: invalid-grid, detection/photo/widget failure, successful replacement and same-snapshot refresh tests. Owned discarded thumbnails/crops are closed under the existing image-ownership contract.

The subject selector required three displayed pixels on both axes, so a 1×1, 2×2 or thin valid image could never be selected. Its minimum now respects each displayed extent, and an explicit Select whole image / Ctrl+A action works before Apply. Normal images retain the minimum-drag threshold. `SubjectSelector.select_subject`; C: real start/drag/apply and Ctrl+A/Return callbacks for tiny/thin images, plus the normal-image rejection and once-only callback assertions. One subject-selection workflow group.

Capturing an unwanted optional calibration point had no remove action. A lone brightness endpoint could make an otherwise valid RGB calibration unsaveable. Exact colour, Paint tool and generic tool dialogs now expose Remove and Start new calibration for the draft. Reset does not delete the saved calibration or bypass the new-capture requirement. `ExactColorCalibration`, `PaintToolCalibration`, `AppToolCalibration`; C: removed brightness can save, removed Brush/opacity fields are absent from the saved payload, generic Clear removal preserves Brush, fresh drafts require recapture, and pending/closed drafts cannot mutate. Repeated implementations count once.

Every progress status rewrite sent the same presentation properties to dozens of widgets. StudioUI now configures only changed properties that it owns, committing its cache after successful Tk calls. Readiness checks and controller-owned Start enablement continue on every refresh. `StudioUI._configure_presentation/_apply_ui_state`; P: 100 actual status-render callbacks keep unchanged configure counts fixed; Start/readiness are still refreshed 101 times. Changed/failed/retried property writes are checked separately. Paired measurement below.

Plus in Fit mode used the sentinel value 0 and could shrink a 100% fitted image to 25%; minus at the explicit minimum could jump back to a larger Fit view. Relative zoom now starts from the visible page's rendered scale and stays monotonic at the supported limits. `PreviewNavigation.relative_zoom`, actual `StudioUI` plus/minus closures; P: fitted scales below/inside/above the explicit range, visible-vs-hidden pages and minimum explicit zoom.

The renderer clamped a viewport but kept the unbounded requested pan. A large drag required hundreds of pixels of reversal before the image moved again. Drag events now store the effective source offset and consume every movement even at an edge; Fit recentres the pages. `PreviewQuality.viewport_geometry`, `PreviewNavigation`, `StudioUI`, root's `DrawBot.show_previews` hook; P: actual drag reversal within one gesture, unchanged edge event, Fit reset, real renderer metadata, and 72 pixel-for-pixel viewport comparisons against the independent baseline formula.

Twelve long horizontal preview tabs exceeded normal centre-panel widths. The active workspace now uses the existing compact page deck with a native keyboard-accessible selector, retaining all twelve named canvases and notifying rendering when the visible page changes. `StudioUI`, `PreviewDeck`; P: page-change callback and Windows narrow-deck registration, selection, width and one-visible-page assertions. Earlier UI05/UI06/IW33 page-registration/rollback optimizations remain the same counted improvements.

Nine Tools actions were packed into one row exceeding 1,000 pixels, making later actions inaccessible in the centre panel. The active Tools row now wraps into a coalesced grid using actual scaled requests and retains every command. `StudioUI`, `ResponsiveRows`; P: uneven-width/scaled-padding column bounds, resize batching/teardown and Windows actual nine-button layout at 100%/150%. One action-row workflow group, not one per button.

The palette table allowed multiple selection, but Remove discarded only its first selected row. Remove/Delete now removes the complete selection from both coordinate and RGB arrays in stable order and focuses the next remaining row. With no selection, the existing last-colour undo remains. `GetColorPositions.undo`; C: noncontiguous selected indices, preserved coordinate/RGB correspondence, next focus, no-selection fallback and closed-dialog guard.

Tall palette and exact-colour forms could put their final controls and Save/Close actions outside a smaller window. These forms now scroll independently above a persistent action footer; Tab focus reveals an off-screen input and the form uses only scoped window bindings. `CalibrationDialogLayout`, `GetColorPositions`, `ExactColorCalibration`; C: local/nested/fractional wheel handling, focus reveal, pending-job cleanup, Windows 650×500 form/footer access and repeated scoped callback teardown. Fitting the outer geometry itself completes IW34 without an extra count.

The main grid imposed 1,096 pixels of column minimums before padding even when the fitted window was narrower, while one-row header/footer controls could be clipped. At narrow widths the same Setup, Workspace and Readiness panels share a native selector; a wide window restores the three columns. Start and Stop remain directly visible, enabled Pause/Resume is promoted, and other actions use a compact menu that reads the existing buttons' live text/state and invokes those same buttons. Header actions use the same mechanism. Workspace and Readiness can scroll at low heights. `ResponsiveWorkspace`, `ResponsiveActionBar`, `StudioUI`, `ResponsiveRows`' native-frame binding bridge; W: width/scaling transitions, focused-panel preservation, header reflow, coalescing/teardown, current menu permissions and late disable, active pause promotion, hidden-focus transfer and exact native CTk frame event binding. The Windows test constructs the complete `DrawBotApp` with NoInput backends at 650×500/1,024×700, 100%/150%, then wide 1,560×960, checking Start/Stop, live overflow state, active Resume and all selected panels. Root's controller integration review passed; all subparts count as one responsive workspace group.

Update checking inspected only the first 100 GitHub releases. A stable release after 100 newer prereleases was reported as absent, and an earlier-created higher semantic version could be missed. `UpdateCenter.check_for_updates` selects the best allowed version across linked pages. It rebuilds every request using the fixed repository endpoint and validated consecutive page numbers, including GitHub's numeric repository-link form. All pages share the existing 30-second cooperative deadline and 16 MiB decoded-body budget, with a ten-page maximum. An incomplete history raises an actionable error instead of claiming the current version is latest. `test_v148_platform_batch06_pagination.py`: real Requests adapter calls cover the 100-prerelease case, semantic selection across three pages, endpoint boundaries, repeated/skipped/ambiguous pages, total size, Stop/deadline and response closure.

Every update attempt downloaded and retained another uniquely named installer, even when identical verified bytes were already present. Successful loose downloads accumulated indefinitely. `InstallerCache` and `UpdateCenter.download_installer` reuse a file only after a complete size/SHA-256/MZ check, and recheck Stop at completion. A cache hit works without network access or additional download space. Cooperating cache operations use a stable file transaction; concurrent completed downloads publish one hash-named installer. Normally retain the current installer and one recently used previous installer in an explicitly marked cache directory. Unknown/unmarked directories, links, other filenames and legacy loose downloads are not adopted or deleted. Busy-file eviction is deferred. `test_v148_platform_batch06_installer_cache.py`: public downloader tests cover repeated reuse, same-size corruption, missing files, cancellation, ownership/links, concurrent publication, locked eviction and inventory failure. The existing Windows locked launcher still rehashes immediately before execution.

Elevated LocalDumps configuration wrote the administrator's already expanded absolute profile path into a machine-wide per-executable setting. An ordinary user running the app could therefore target another account's dump folder. `CrashDumpConfig` writes the expandable `REG_EXPAND_SZ` value `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ImageDrawBot\dumps`; normal Windows app startup prepares its own account's folder and diagnostics inventories that same location. An already owned absolute setting can migrate without losing the original undo values. A validated transitional `previous_written` record permits Disable to recover after partial native writes or a final undo-file publication failure, while preserving later external registry changes. The existing full preflight and transaction remain. `test_v148_platform_batch06_diagnostics.py`: two-account path expansion, normal startup/report inventory, undo-before-migration and failure injection at each native write plus final publication.

Invalid UTF-8 in a local dependency's real `METADATA` file caused `importlib.metadata.version` to abort the entire diagnostics ZIP, losing otherwise readable logs and other package versions. `DiagnosticsPackage._package_versions` contains ordinary per-distribution read/metadata failures. `system.json` records the affected fixed package name and exception class in `collection_issues`; raw exception messages, local paths and credentials are not copied. Missing optional packages retain their existing normal omission behavior, and cancellation is not swallowed. Public archive tests use a real malformed `PathDistribution` and verify retained session logs, other package versions and privacy-safe failure details.

The standalone diagnostics helper reported collection failure and returned exit code 1 when Explorer could not open the folder, even though the complete ZIP was already saved. `DiagnosticsPackage.main` separates archive creation from folder presentation. Successful publication retains exit code 0 and the concrete saved path when automatic opening fails; the windowed frozen helper also shows the saved path in a notice. A real public-main regression creates and validates the ZIP, injects the shell-open failure and checks success, console result and windowed notice.

Importing a real unsigned 16-bit grayscale PNG containing values `0, 257, 32768, 65535` produced 8-bit gray values `0, 255, 255, 255`. The direct Pillow conversion clipped most of the tonal range. `SourcePixelDepth.grayscale_8bit` maps the fixed unsigned range to `0, 1, 128, 255` using nearest rounding. File and borrowed bitmap-clipboard input pass through this conversion after EXIF orientation and before any ICC transform. Transparency keys are compared at their original precision, so adjacent values that become the same 8-bit tone retain different opacity. The source label identifies the conversion. Tests read real PNG and both-endian TIFF files, compare all 65,536 input values against an independent rounding oracle, exercise a real transparent PNG with and without a valid gray ICC profile, orientation, the actual clipboard handler, ownership and cancellation.

Recording durations were first rounded to integer milliseconds and then independently truncated to GIF's 10 ms units. One hundred changing frames captured for 259 ms each encoded as 25,000 ms rather than 25,900 ms. Retain fractional capture milliseconds until encoding; quantize cumulative frame boundaries to the GIF clock. Every boundary stays within 5 ms of the recorded timeline instead of accumulating truncation loss. Decode real GIFs to verify exact frame colors, variable durations, half-tick boundaries and identical-frame merging. An actual `record_screen` worker with a controlled capture clock retains a 25,949 ms recording as 25,950 ms. Timing validation occurs before staging and preserves an existing file on invalid input.

The recorder retained every quantized frame until the final GIF encoder, even when adjacent captures were identical and Pillow would later merge them. A static 100-frame 800×500 recording retained 40,000,000 bytes of paletted pixel payload. Coalesce exact adjacent captures during recording, summing their raw durations and releasing duplicate owned images immediately. Compare dimensions, mode, RGBA palette, transparency and pixel indexes; an identical index with another palette cannot merge. The static fixture retains one frame/400,000 pixel bytes. Changing footage still retains every distinct frame. Actual-worker tests verify early duplicate release, failure cleanup and the final decoded visible timeline.

Deadline importance sampled stored vertices, so reversing or subdividing an unchanged path could alter its priority, phase and protection. A two-endpoint line also omitted every interior pixel. In an actual source fixture, reversing the same segment changed importance from about 0.391 to 0.841 and changed an optional accuracy stroke into a protected structure stroke. Stream canonical forward/reverse geometry, remove redundant forward-collinear vertices while preserving turns and backtracking, and sample up to 24 locations at uniform arc-length intervals. Pixel coordinates are deduplicated; the existing mean/high-percentile weighting remains.

Shadow analysis copied already-owned float32 luminance/blur/gradient planes and a second full set of five published guidance maps. Transfer the existing owned float32 planes without redundant `astype` copies. Output planes remain independent of borrowed inputs; formulas and dtype remain unchanged.

Initial deadline admission debited every custom selector before any path was admitted, including empty/unselected colors. A real 32-color, 30-second plan admitted zero paths even though a useful subset fit. The later ordered-cost gate could remove overbudget paths but could not recover candidates rejected at this earlier stage. Keep unconditional preparation overhead separate from conditional color costs. Debit palette/custom/adaptive-verification setup only when the first path using a color is admitted, then retain the final ordered delivery gate. Empty groups and current-color-only plans do not buy unused color controls.

Both fast browser rasterizers unconditionally excluded supplied white groups, even after the source planner had deliberately retained white ink or correction strokes with Skip white disabled. White variants could also be mapped into a colored swatch or lose short fragments. Preserve explicit supplied white geometry, retain a white anchor within the color ceiling, map white variants only to retained white, and prevent white gap joining or minimum-run pruning. Source white-skipping stays with the upstream source mask.

Background simplification retained a Python `(x,y)` tuple for every reached pixel alongside its existing visited mask, then copied its private RGB image before applying exactly those pixels. Retain only the component count during traversal. After the unchanged coverage gate, scan membership spans from the existing byte mask and update the owned RGB conversion. Eliminate the full coordinate list and second RGB image copy.

Gartic's dual-axis choice ranked only surviving stroke cost. With minimum run 2, a 36-pixel horizontal blue line was pruned into zero vertical candidates; the empty candidate won as cheaper and deleted the line. Rotating the source caused the corresponding horizontal loss. Compare retained original-pixel coverage first, then the existing stroke-count and pen-distance cost. Count source interval unions and exclude pixels invented by gap bridging. Preserve the original vertical storage ceiling and minimum-fragment policy.

Application-created CustomTkinter buttons had pointer bindings but no consistent Tab traversal or Return/Space activation. Decorative labels could acquire their own focus stops through tooltip bindings. `UiKeyboardNavigation.KeyboardButton` gives each live, mapped, enabled action one outer-frame Tab stop and a visible focus outline. Return, keypad Enter and Space invoke the existing button command once on release; autorepeat, focus loss, hidden/disabled controls and destruction cannot deliver a stale activation. Focus reveals the target through owned nested CTk scroll frames, and activation rechecks that its centre remains inside every viewport. Tooltips receive that logical focus while retaining pointer behavior. `StudioUI.button`, inline setting help and `UICompactLayout.CompactGroup` use the local subclass. K executes the inherited CTk `invoke()` with live states, cancellation and repeated-event sequences; actual tooltip callbacks and vertical/horizontal/nested/failing scroll models cover integration. Three Windows tests verify real Tk traversal, recreated labels, key delivery, focus rendering/tooltips, Tab-to-bottom visibility, owned Tcl-command deletion, unchanged global bindings and the actual controller's Start setup guard. One shared button-interaction group, not one per key or widget.

The generic error card's Retry action always called `draw(test=True, user_initiated=True)`, even for an image import, disk-write or GPU failure. It could request drawing unrelated to the failed operation. The card now offers Help. `StudioUI.show_error_help` reads the current classified error and displays its explanation and next step; resolved errors and shutdown do nothing. W extracts and executes the actual card callback for storage, import, GPU and palette errors, checks the live error after a status change, and asserts that drawing, Quick Start and worker methods are never called. Existing dedicated correction/retry workflows are unchanged.

A native combobox selection event for the already active profile still saved settings, cleared the plan/area/resume and disarmed the drawing state. Choosing the same profile therefore discarded valid setup despite no configuration change. `DrawBot.change_profile` treats an already active selection as a no-op and cancels an outstanding queued switch when the user returns to the active profile. The explicit internal `_apply_profile_change` path remains available for Import/Reset to reload that same profile. P calls the actual methods and verifies preservation of plan, area, resume, paths and permissions; no save/disarm; cancellation of the previous callback; and continued forced reload behavior. Root owns this implementation and its tests; it is counted only in this UI ledger.

The UI advertised Sketch + Auto Fill, and its Paint renderer existed, but `DrawBot.options` rejected that selection as an invalid rendering style. Reading saved settings silently left Auto instead of restoring it. Both existing rendering-style membership checks now include the already imported `SKETCH_FILL_RENDER_STYLE`. R reproduces the three failures before the change, then runs the actual Paint `options` → `make_plan` chain and verifies its ordered sketch/color-fill/re-outline sequence, actual save/read restoration, continued browser-target restriction and rejection of unknown style names. This is one advertised-renderer activation/persistence group; it does not change UP01's automatic profile policy or the renderer algorithm.

Starting mobile preview or accepting another plan synchronously resized, flattened and encoded all three PNGs on the Tk callback. Even an unchanged Original was recompressed for each plan. Equality was checked only after encoding. `MobilePreviewServer.queue_images` captures owned snapshots on the image-owning thread and uses `MobilePreviewQueue.LatestImageQueue`: one encoder and one latest pending request. Unchanged immutable identities skip capture/encoding, individual unchanged views reuse their encoded bytes, and aliased views share one snapshot/PNG. Requests reserve generation/sequence before capture; superseded work cannot publish. Capture and encoder failures close owned buffers and allow an identical request to retry. The synchronous `update_images` API still rereads mutable inputs. `test_v148_platform_batch07_mobile_queue.py` and `_mobile_snapshots.py` exercise real PIL images, races, cleanup while exception tracebacks remain referenced, cancellation, thread construction/start failure, source mutation/closure after capture, weak identities, exact PNG parity and the actual memory limit.

Several accepted source changes and plan invalidations never notified mobile preview. In Manual mode, Undo could restore a red desktop Original and clear its plan while the phone indefinitely retained the previous blue image and old plan. Root's `DrawBot._sync_mobile_preview` coalesces a single Tk-idle callback, which reads current `PreviewViews` only when it runs. `show_previews`, `_mark_plan_stale` and existing adoption paths cover accepted source changes, settings/profile invalidation and new plans. Missing views are explicitly cleared. Mobile stop cancels the pending callback, invalidates its ticket and retains the server instance for restart, so an old native encode does not create a second independent encoder owner. Ordinary drawing Stop does not suppress already accepted images. `test_v148_application_batch07_mobile.py` exercises the real Undo and load handlers, Manual invalidation, current-state coalescing, display-layer selection, stale callbacks, session replacement/shutdown and safe retry after capture failure.

Public image import tried every Pillow plugin. An EPS document named `.png`, labeled `image/png` in a data URL, or returned as `image/png` over HTTP reached Pillow's Ghostscript renderer even though the application advertises raster-image input. This renderer was outside the import worker's cooperative Stop handling. `ImageImport.read_image` passes an explicit raster-format tuple to `Image.open`, preserving PNG/APNG, JPEG/MPO, WEBP, BMP/DIB, GIF, TIFF, ICO and AVIF. Unsupported documents/vector formats get a useful export-to-raster message before a document decoder or renderer runs. Four policy regression tests in `test_v148_platform_batch07_image_decoders.py` exercise local/data/HTTP EPS and WMF rejection with mocked renderer boundaries, all advertised raster decoders, AVIF, animated PNG and actual two-frame MPO files. Existing ICC, unsigned 16-bit, orientation, pixel/byte budgets and cancellation stay in place.

A successful background-removal cut copied its already-private, oriented RGBA source a second time immediately before replacing alpha. That full-image allocation served no remaining consumer; a 320×240 cut copied 614,400 bytes of RGBA pixel payload across two copies. Transfer the existing private buffer into the result after all cut/safety checks and write its final alpha there. Borrowed input remains unchanged. Independent expected pixels, RGB/RGBA and partial alpha, EXIF orientation, no-op, Stop and alpha-write failure regressions verify the ownership transfer and cleanup. Successful cut fixtures now make one full RGBA copy (307,200 bytes), while no-op fixtures retain their existing single copy.

Every ordinary desktop preview redraw recomputed the visible bitmap and uploaded it to Tk, even when the same immutable accepted image, viewport and canvas were unchanged. Repeating the actual `show_previews` call performed two rasterizations/uploads per image. Each canvas retains one bitmap keyed by a weak source identity, source mode and normalized viewport geometry. Repeated accepted-image redraws reuse that bitmap; replacement sources, zoom/pan/size changes, closed sources, hidden/destroyed canvases and construction failures invalidate it. Owned intermediate viewport images close after Tk copies their data. The actual controller test retains Original across a new plan and rerenders only the changed result. Public `viewport_image` retains its fresh-render contract for arbitrary mutable callers.
Respect the selected CPU/Auto/explicit GPU policy in both regional PixelMap reconstructions and the benchmark caller; actual CPU planning cannot open a saved preferred OpenCL backend.
Calculate source contrast from visible, white-composited pixels and restore original alpha; hidden RGB no longer changes visible drawing colors while opaque and identity results stay exact.
Replace per-offset full-ROI square brush shifts with exact separable rolling reductions and bounded numeric work storage, preserving even-brush geometry, Stop and executable results.

Convert detected cell-edge Fill polygons to executable pixel-center contours with safe concave bridges and reachable interior seeds; unchanged flood/halo gates preserve fallback and final reports reflect accepted regions.
